findings.claim: The constructor now wraps reportDiagnostic in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in source or not in this compilation. Any diagnostic previously reported with Location.None (null location resolves to None) is now silently suppressed. Examples are MsgPack004 on a member inherited from a base type in a referenced assembly, and diagnostics whose syntax lookup returns null. Users who relied on these errors (MsgPack003/004/005 are Errors) stop seeing them. That is a behavior change beyond the crash fix, and the requirement asked only that the crash be avoided.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: a [MessagePackObject] class in the compiling assembly derives from a base class in a referenced assembly. The base has a public property without [Key]. Run with base and head builds and compare the MsgPack004 diagnostic. If head reports nothing where base reported a diagnostic with Location.None, the finding is confirmed. Also repeat with a metadata-only member that previously produced a location-less error.

findings.claim: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic now passes a null location when FirstOrDefault() finds no syntax. Diagnostic.Create with a null location becomes Location.None, and the new filter then drops it. For metadata members the diagnostic is therefore lost, with no error and no fallback to the derived type's identifier. For inherited members without [Key] this removes an error-level MsgPack004 that existed before whenever the location was valid. This is only a hunch from reading the code.

receipt_plan.detail: Read TypeCollector.cs around line 1077 and ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. Confirm that a null location becomes Location.None, which is not IsInSource, so the diagnostic is discarded.

questions.text: When a diagnostic's offending member or type has no source location in the compiling assembly (an inherited member from a referenced assembly, or a metadata symbol), should it be dropped, or reported against the derived type's identifier?
options: Drop it, since the defining assembly owns validation
Report it at the identifier of the type in the compiling assembly that contains or inherits the member
questions.why_it_matters: If dropping is intended, the blanket filter is acceptable and the findings above are not defects. If reporting is intended, error-level diagnostics such as MsgPack004 for inherited members now silently vanish, which is a user-visible regression.
